observations: Piray 2026 CAUSE remains an arXiv preprint dated 2026-05-19. It formally distinguishes latent volatility from observation stochasticity and maps them to opposite exploration pressure; the paper reports CAUSE outperforming standard exploration strategies in heterogeneous-noise restless Gaussian state-space bandits and matching Gittins within Monte Carlo error in the rested limit.

Fresh web and GitHub searches for the exact title, arXiv id 2605.19215, and CAUSE bandit terminology did not locate an author reference implementation or a clear independent execution/replication. GitHub hits for the arXiv id were RSS/news/reference mirrors rather than implementation evidence.
public_source_update.code_replication_status: No author reference implementation or clear independent CAUSE rerun found in this run; absence of discovery is not evidence that none exists.

bounded_audit.scope: Source-derived synthetic audit continuing the prior variance/covariance identifiability branch. This is not an exact reproduction of CAUSE, Piray-Daw, SPLiT, PAST/GROUSE, or the predecessor four-state duration controller. The source learner is a calibrated window-level grid/pseudo-posterior moment learner, not yet a full online event-level Bayesian filter.

source_learner.model: Observed prediction-error-like sequence is decomposed as two persistent components with autocovariance gamma_l = Q*a^l + S*rho^l. A semantic prior anchors latent persistence a near 0.82 while rho is broader; Q and S are nonnegative moment amplitudes. The learner profiles multiple lags, computes a Jacobian/conditioning diagnostic, and may abstain rather than force a volatility/stochasticity label.
source_learner.calibration: Disjoint calibration seeds selected a profile-evidence gap threshold 0.60 as the highest-coverage tested threshold with zero confident calibration errors across clean separated, Gaussian ambiguous, high-noise volatility and correlated-burst stochasticity cases. A non-Gaussian gate uses Gaussian-calibration 99th-percentile absolute-skew 0.3109 or excess-kurtosis 0.4587 before activating a separately calibrated higher-order classifier trained on Student-t5/lognormal observation-source signatures.

heldout_stress.interpretation: The identifiability gate converts the main failure mode from confident semantic reversal into abstention. Strong skew can recover useful source information in many ill-conditioned windows; Student-t5 tails are much less decisive at this sample size. The cost is substantial coverage loss for volatility-dominant cases, so this is a safety gate rather than a high-recall source estimator.

decision_layer.design: A separate 4-arm restless Gaussian bandit probe used the published CAUSE closed-form structure in a source-derived implementation. True arms span high/low volatility and high/low observation stochasticity. K=4, T=250, 1500 paired seeds; v_low=0.01, v_high=0.5, s_low=0.25, s_high=12.0. Regret is undiscounted latent pseudo-regret, not the paper's discounted cumulative regret. Policies: oracle source parameters; categorical source reversal; and shared/base fallback using the same pooled v and s for all arms, which removes source-specific exploration pressure.
decision_layer.interpretation: In this bounded regime, source reversal is materially worse than falling back to a shared/base source model. The shared fallback does not recover oracle performance, but it avoids about 39 regret units of the additional cost caused by reversed attribution. This directly supports abstention as a decision-safety action when volatility versus stochasticity is not identifiable.

mechanistic_interpretation.positive: Cause-aware uncertainty is valuable only when the cause is identifiable. An explicit conditioning/profile-evidence gate can prevent the exact failure CAUSE predicts—reversed exploration under source misattribution—and a shared/base fallback can be substantially less damaging than a confident reversal. Higher-order evidence can selectively reopen decisions when observation sources carry a stable non-Gaussian signature, especially strong skew.
mechanistic_interpretation.negative_boundary: The current learner is conservative and window-based. It abstains on 60% of clean volatility windows and more than 90% of Student-t5 ambiguous stochasticity windows. It also has not yet been integrated online so detection delay, posterior calibration and feedback loops with action selection are unresolved. The CAUSE decision probe uses source-derived formulas and synthetic parameter levels, not author code or paper-matched benchmark regimes.

bounded_audit.comparison_to_predecessor: The predecessor matched four-state controller remains the strongest role-local event-level duration/noise baseline under its own synthetic family (e.g. stable-overdispersion false activation 0.78% and ~20-46 event clean-change delays). This run did not force a numeric head-to-head because the new AR-component identifiability learner operates on a different observation model; treating those numbers as directly comparable would overstate evidence.

limits: The latent-persistence prior is informative and narrows semantic label symmetry; performance without such an anchor is weaker.
The higher-order classifier is calibrated only on Gaussian, Student-t5 and centered-lognormal families and must not be generalized to arbitrary heavy tails or skew.
The held-out stress uses fixed-length windows and does not measure online change latency.
The CAUSE regret experiment uses undiscounted latent pseudo-regret and a source-derived implementation, not the paper's exact simulation code or discounted metric.
No source-exact PAST/GROUSE or SPLiT execution occurred.
